entries.words: I have heard nothing worth repeating.

The talk at the Greenspring lodge is that more cult couriers and sap-tappers are passing through on the way to Helstrom than anyone remembers. The lodge-keeper swears a few of the quiet ones are Veiled Reed factors, the covert agents of the An-Xileel, keeping an eye on who comes and goes.
Salt is reaching the Greenspring spring from the salt works upstream. The village blames the works for it. At the lodge, the other talk is of who will carry the next load to Helstrom.

Travellers through Greenspring say that a Hist in the south has gone silent. That means the tree has stopped speaking to its tribe. A Hist can fall silent when it is sick or when it shuts itself off from the other Hist.
Talk in the gang's camp is that more adults go downriver on the roll each year. The roll is the list of debtors in the dredging gang. It is read out on the barge, never in the camp.

Travellers through Greenspring say that cutters have been working at the edge of a Hist grove inland. A grove is a stand of the great trees that have minds. The minders of the Conclave keep such trees.

The Mile House says a pardon and a wage may come from Gideon for the men of the column. The same talk says the governor will not pay to clear the camp. It also says the toll company would sooner hire the men than pay them off.
